patterns.name: Ranked horizontal bar
patterns.reader_question: Which entity is largest on one measure, and by how much?
patterns.relationship: Magnitude ranking of comparable entities on a single measure and status.
use_when: Every bar shares one unit, one definition and one status (for example committed, not announced)
Rank order itself matters to the argument
avoid_when: Values mix statuses or bases — use status-separated-capital or parallel-basis-panels
Fewer than three entities — state the comparison in the title or use a two-value callout

data_contract.notes: Measure, unit and status, shown as the series name

patterns.units: One unit and status for every bar; zero baseline.

editable: Bar values and labels through Edit Data (embedded workbook)
Bar colours, gap width, data-label format
Frame text: title, subtitle, interpretation, source
not_data_bound: Highlight colour is a per-point fill; re-sorting after a data edit is manual

patterns.table_alternative: A two-column table (entity, value) when exact figures matter more than rank, or when there are more than twelve entities.
variations: Vertical columns for up to six short labels
Ranked dot plot (ranked-dot) when bars would be visually heavy
limitations: Does not show uncertainty, status mix or change over time

excluded_alternatives.reason: Angles compare magnitudes less accurately than aligned bar lengths and fail beyond a few categories
Perspective distorts length; prohibited by the exhibit rules

patterns.name: Two-observation dumbbell
patterns.reader_question: How did each entity change between two comparable observations?
patterns.relationship: Paired observations per entity on a shared axis; the gap is the change.
use_when: Both observations use the same population, definition and unit
The size of each change matters more than the rank
avoid_when: More than two time points — use annotated-line or small-multiples
The second value is a target or forecast — mark it as such or use evidence-milestone-strip

data_contract.notes: Names of the two observations (for example period labels)
Shared axis maximum; must cover every value

patterns.units: One unit and population for both observations; axis starts at zero.

editable: Every dot, connector and label is a native shape or text box (move, recolour, retype)
not_data_bound: Positions are computed from the fixture; changing a value means moving the shape or re-running the renderer — there is no Edit Data

patterns.table_alternative: A three-column table (entity, first, second, change) when exact values are needed.
variations: Slope chart (slope) when rank reversal is the point
Paired bars (grouped-bar) for two series with few entities
limitations: Endpoints are observations; the connector does not represent the path between them

excluded_alternatives.reason: Cannot show per-entity change and compares angles across charts

patterns.name: Reconciling waterfall bridge
patterns.reader_question: How did an opening balance become the closing balance, and which movements drove it?
patterns.relationship: Additive reconciliation: opening + Σ movements = closing, on one consistent basis.
use_when: Opening and closing balances share a basis and every movement is stated
The size and sign of each driver matters
avoid_when: Movements do not reconcile or are on different bases — use parallel-basis-panels
Movements are scenario sensitivities rather than additive changes — use tornado

data_contract.notes: Closing balance; must equal start + Σ deltas

patterns.units: One unit throughout; bars keep true geometry (no inflated small movements).

editable: Stacked bar chart with embedded workbook (Edit Data)
not_data_bound: The unfilled 'helper' series holds each float; editing a movement requires recomputing the helper column
Connector hairlines between bars are native shapes positioned from the fixture

patterns.table_alternative: A reconciliation table (line item, movement, running balance) for audit-grade lookup.
limitations: Running balances must stay non-negative for the helper-series geometry
Movements are read in sequence; the order is a presentation choice, not causation

excluded_alternatives.form: Stacked bar of opening and closing only
excluded_alternatives.reason: Hides which movements produced the change
Implies flow between nodes rather than an additive balance

patterns.name: Sources and uses
patterns.reader_question: Where does a financing package come from, and what does it pay for?
patterns.relationship: Two stacked columns that reconcile: Σ sources = Σ uses.
use_when: A single package has stated sources and stated uses that total the same amount
The split between public, private and debt sources matters
avoid_when: Sources and uses do not reconcile — show the gap explicitly or use parallel-basis-panels
Components mix committed and conditional capital — use status-separated-capital
patterns.units: One currency and time basis for both sides.

editable: Stacked column chart with embedded workbook (Edit Data)
Component labels are native text boxes
not_data_bound: Side labels and totals are text boxes positioned from the fixture; update them if values change

patterns.table_alternative: A two-block table (sources with amounts, uses with amounts, matching totals).
variations: Percent-stacked columns when only shares matter
limitations: Does not show timing or conditions of each source

excluded_alternatives.reason: Hides the reconciliation and compares angles
Implies source-to-use allocation that the package rarely states
